title: Linear combinations and span
terms: linear combination; span; spanning set; trivial linear combination.

exposition.text:
A linear combination of v , . . . , v is a v + · · · + a v . Their span is the set of all such combina-
1 k 1 1 k k
tions, the smallest subspace containing them. Membership in a span becomes a linear system
with the spanning vectors as columns and the target as right-hand side.
Adding a vector already in the span changes neither the span nor its dimension. Replacing one
vector by itself plus a multiple of another preserves the span; multiplying a vector by a nonzero
scalar does too. These facts underlie elimination. The span of the empty set is conventionally
{0}. A spanning set can contain substantial redundancy.
The trivial linear combination is the one with every coefficient zero. A span uses arbitrary
scalars and finite sums, so even nonnegative generators can span functions of either sign. One
always has span(S ∩ T) ⊆ span S ∩ span T, but equality can fail.

question.text:
For what a is (1, a, 3) in the span of (1, 1, 0) and (0, 1, 1)?
(A) −2 (B) 0 (C) 2 (D) 3 (E) 4

solution.text:
A combination is (s, s + t, t). Matching the first and third entries forces s = 1, t = 3, hence
the middle entry must be a = 4.
